Google Search.text: Despite its huge index, it is generally assumed to cover less than 5% of the total Internet.
Google Search.evidence: Despite Google search's immense index, sources generally assume that Google is only indexing less than 5% of the total Internet, with the rest belonging to the deep web, inaccessible through its search tools.

YouTube.text: By 2019, more than 500 hours of video were being uploaded to it every minute.
YouTube.evidence: As of May 2019, videos were being uploaded to the platform at a rate of more than 500 hours of video per minute, and as of mid-2024, there were approximately 14.8 billion videos in total.

Facebook.text: Its name comes from the face book directories often given to American university students.
Facebook.evidence: The name Facebook derives from the face book directories often given to American university students.

Instagram.text: It began in San Francisco as Burbn, a mobile check-in app.
Instagram.evidence: Instagram began development in San Francisco as Burbn, a mobile check-in app created by Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger.

ChatGPT.text: It reached 100 million monthly active users two months after its release.
ChatGPT.evidence: ChatGPT was quickly adopted, reaching 100 million monthly active users two months after its release and 900 million weekly active users in February 2026.

X.text: It launched in 2006 as twttr, and was renamed Twitter some months later.
X.evidence: The platform was created in March 2006 by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone, and Evan Williams, and was launched in July of that year; initially named twttr, it was renamed Twitter some months later.

Reddit.text: Its founders' first pitch, My Mobile Menu, was a failed idea for ordering food by text message.
Reddit.evidence: Their initial idea, My Mobile Menu, was unsuccessful, and was intended to allow users to order food by SMS text messaging.

TikTok.text: TikTok Ltd is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and based in both Singapore and Los Angeles.
TikTok.evidence: TikTok Ltd was incorporated in the Cayman Islands in the Caribbean and is based in both Singapore and Los Angeles.

WhatsApp.text: When early versions kept crashing, Jan Koum considered giving up until Brian Acton urged him to wait.
WhatsApp.evidence: However, when early versions of WhatsApp kept crashing, Koum considered giving up and looking for a new job. Acton encouraged him to wait for a "few more months".

Microsoft Bing.text: About 27% of its monthly global traffic comes from China, more than from the United States.
Microsoft Bing.evidence: Approximately 27.43% of Bing's monthly global traffic comes from China, 22.16% from the United States, 4.85% from Japan, 4.18% from Germany and 3.61% from France.
